rationale: 4-22x faster install+test vs Node.js. CI is a sandboxed environment so observability/debugging gaps are non-blocking. Fintech case study: 84% CI time reduction. Risk is low.
caveats: Use oven/bun:1.1-slim for Docker. Verify Playwright compatibility if used. Stay on Node.js for production runtime unless observability tooling is not required.

rationale: 40% lower memory (K8s savings), 4x faster cold start (serverless fit). Anthropic uses it for Claude Code CLI. But APM support is experimental and native addons break.
caveats: Do not use if service depends on Datadog/New Relic/Sentry SDKs, bcrypt/sharp, or HTTP/2 pipelining. Greenfield microservices and serverless functions are the sweet spot.

item: React Server Components as default for new projects
rationale: RSC is the default execution model in Next.js App Router and React 19. Bundle reduction of 30-50% for content-heavy apps. Eliminates useEffect waterfalls. Industry consensus: no longer optional knowledge.
caveats: Three carve-outs: highly interactive apps (Figma-like), offline-first PWAs, simple static sites. Tailwind-heavy components may benefit from Client Component marking to reduce Flight payload size. Framework lock-in to Next.js is the practical reality.

decision: Mandatory — plan and execute by priority
rationale: Express 4 entered Maintenance April 2025, EOL target October 2026. Compliance frameworks (SOC 2, FedRAMP, HIPAA, DORA) flag unsupported dependencies as open findings. Express 3 already EOL shows the project follows through. Migration is real work: 3 weeks to 3 months per service, $50k-$250k per service at enterprise scale.
caveats: Upgrade Node.js to 22 first. Audit third-party middleware compatibility. Reconfigure req.query parser if you rely on nested query params. Renamed methods (sendfile→sendFile, del→delete) need search-and-replace. If calendar extends past Oct 2026, secure commercial extended-support bridge. This is also a natural inflection point to evaluate Fastify/Hono/serverless as alternatives.
